answer: Cross-epoch pulse matching. Each epoch an agent emits a signed pulse; the protocol derives a beacon from its history of pulse timing and interaction partners. New identities lacking prior pulses get a cold-start weight, so a fresh identity’s first interaction costs it a full probing round delay plus forfeited accrued jade rewards from the null prior epoch. Maintaining N identities means sustaining N distinct pulse histories across epochs or losing weight, so the attacker pays continuous coordination and delay, not a one-time fee.
